title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Company Personnel
tiers.description: The Board, officers and employees (including permanent, contract, secondment and long-term agency staff, and consultants) of the Company or any of its insiders or affiliates (including subsidiaries), associates of such persons, and any other insider who may be in possession of or have access to confidential, material information regarding the Company. All Closed Period, blackout, exceptional-circumstances, encumbrance and pre-trading approval rules apply to this base tier.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors, including the Managing Director; distinguished for approval routing (requests addressed to the Chair) and for the additional duty to report every trade, acquisition, disposal or agreement to enter a future transaction to the Corporate Secretary within 2 business days, and the Company's own 5-business-day ASX reporting obligation for Director trades.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The Board Chair; distinguished only for approval routing, since requests by the Chair are addressed to the Chair of the Audit Committee (or, for exceptional-circumstances determinations, an independent non-executive Director) instead of to the Chair.

tiers.name: Family Members and Associates
tiers.description: Family members and others living in the Company Personnel member's household who gain access to undisclosed material information (the Company Personnel member is responsible for their compliance), plus, per the signed acknowledgement, all family members, holding companies and other related entities expected to comply with the Policy.

windows.start_anchor: not less than the two week period prior to the anticipated date of release of the Company's half yearly accounts
windows.end_anchor: commencement of trading on the business day following release (or, if released after close of trading, the next business day)

windows.start_anchor: not less than the two week period prior to the anticipated date of release of the Company's annual accounts
windows.end_anchor: commencement of trading on the business day following release (or, if released after close of trading, the next business day)

windows.start_anchor: not less than the two week period prior to the anticipated date of release of the Company's quarterly activities & cashflow reports
windows.end_anchor: commencement of trading on the business day following release (or, if released after close of trading, the next business day)

windows.start_anchor: release of a market sensitive announcement made between less than one hour prior to market open and prior to market close
windows.end_anchor: three hours after release of the announcement, or the following trading day if less than three hours remain between release and market close

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may determine any other period to be a Closed Period. Separately, the CEO or designate (after consulting legal counsel) can approve exceptions to 'blackout periods' imposed on personnel with access to undisclosed material information in the normal course of duties (see the Company's Corporate Disclosure Policy s.3.6); personnel are 'prohibited from communicating (tipping) internally or externally to anyone else that the Company is subject to a blackout period', making the existence of a blackout confidential.

rules.detail: 'Securities' is defined as the Company's own listed securities (including CDIs); the Policy does not state that dealing/trading extends to OTC derivatives written over those securities by a third party.
No hedging or 'limiting economic risk' provision appears anywhere in the Policy.

Monetisation is not named. Directors must report 'any agreement to enter into a future transaction' and prior written approval to trade is required for all periods, so a forward sale or similar monetisation is caught as trading requiring approval.
rules.evidence: any trade, acquisition or disposal (directly or indirectly) of an interest in the Company's Securities as soon as practicable ... or any agreement to enter into a future transaction, with full details of the transaction.

rules.detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.
CFDs are not mentioned anywhere in the Policy.

Margin lending is named as an example of a secured lending arrangement. Entering one is 'trading' requiring the standing prior written approval process (section 7), but a margin lender's forced sale on default is expressly excluded from the Closed Period ban and needs no separate approval.
rules.evidence: A disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: Encumbering Securities is expressly named and approvable even during a Closed Period, provided the person is not in possession of Inside Information and (in a Closed Period) exceptional circumstances are found by the Chair or an independent non-executive Director.
rules.evidence: Company Personnel who are not in possession of Inside Information may also apply for and be given written approval to encumber Securities.

rules.detail: No blanket ban; any secured financing arrangement involving Company Securities is approvable as encumbrance (section 8), and a secured lender's enforcement is not itself a Policy breach (6(g)).
rules.evidence: Company Personnel who are not in possession of Inside Information may also apply for and be given written approval to encumber Securities.

rules.detail: No holding-period, intention test or short-swing trading rule appears in the Policy.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: promptly following completion of any trade
clearance.evidence: Approval, if granted, must be in writing (which can be by email) and will specify a time limit for which the approval applies. ... automatically deemed: (a) to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of any Inside Information ... (b) suspended upon the start of any Closed Period

clearance.approver: Chair (for other Directors, including the Managing Director)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as practicable, and in any event within 2 business days
clearance.evidence: all Directors must report to the Corporate Secretary any trade, acquisition or disposal (directly or indirectly) of an interest in the Company's Securities as soon as practicable (and in any event within 2 business days) after such transaction

clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as practicable, and in any event within 2 business days
clearance.evidence: If the Chair is the Company Personnel, the request for written approval shall be addressed to the Chair of the Audit Committee as the decision maker.

exceptions.evidence: Transfer of Securities already held in a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Company Personnel is a beneficiary, but the Company Personnel has no control or influence over the investment decisions
Transfer of Securities where there is no change in any beneficial interest, for example upon the change of trustee of a trust where the Securities are property of the trust
Undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer

An investment in, or trading units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party

Where the relevant member of Company Personnel is a trustee, trading in Securities by that trust provided the Company Personnel member is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Closed Period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently

Trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution investment plan (DRP) and an equal access buy-back
A disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement
Receipt of Securities for which shareholder approval has been obtained
The issue of Securities upon the conversion of convertible securities (i.e. exercise of options, conversion of performance rights etc)
Receipt of Securities pursuant to an incentive scheme of the Company where the offer of such Securities is either made on a periodic basis or the offer was made or accepted outside a Closed Period

exceptions.approver: Chair or an independent non-executive Director
exceptions.evidence: The exercise (but not the sale of Securities following exercise) of an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme ... where the Company Personnel could not ... reasonably have exercised the options at a time prior to the Closed Period

Trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided ... The trading plan does not permit the Company Personnel to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade

exceptions.approver: Chair, or an independent non-executive Director if the Chair is the applicant
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship which means a person has a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the Securities

exceptions.approver: Chair, or an independent non-executive Director if the Chair is the applicant
exceptions.evidence: if a person is required by a court order, or there are court enforceable undertakings to transfer or sell the Securities or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement for the person to do so

exceptions.approver: Chair, or an independent non-executive Director if the Chair is the applicant
exceptions.evidence: a situation determined by the Chair ... to be an exceptional circumstance

financing_disclosure: Directors: after entering into any transaction or agreement to enter a future transaction affecting an interest in the Company's Securities (which would include granting security over them), to the Corporate Secretary, as soon as practicable and in any event within 2 business days.

external_documents: Corporate Disclosure Policy (section 3.6, on blackout periods)
exemption_authority: The Chair (or, if the Chair is the applicant, an independent non-executive Director, or a majority of the rest of the Board) determines in their sole and absolute discretion whether 'exceptional circumstances' (severe financial hardship, court order/legal requirement, or any other situation the Chair considers exceptional) justify approving a sale, disposal or encumbrance during a Closed Period. The CEO or designate, after consulting legal counsel, may grant exceptions to a 'blackout period'.
jurisdiction_overlays: Canadian securities law (Reporting Insider / SEDI insider reporting obligations)

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no provision restricting hedging, or transactions that limit the economic risk of a security holding.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar's derivative legs are not caught by any hedging-specific prohibition; they are governed only by the general prior-written-approval process for 'trading' and, for the loan leg, the encumbrance approval process.

bespoke_clauses.topic: encumbrance approvable even in a Closed Period
bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Personnel who are not in possession of Inside Information may also apply for and be given written approval to encumber Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar can be secured on the shares even inside a Closed Period, subject to a case-by-case approval, which is unusually permissive compared with policies that ban secured financing outright.

bespoke_clauses.topic: lender enforcement excluded from Closed Period ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: A disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is Excluded Trading, completed] without seeking prior approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale on default or margin call is not itself a Policy breach and needs no fresh clearance, even during a Closed Period, reducing the bank's execution risk on default.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any prior written approval to trade in Securities ... is automatically deemed: (a) to be withdrawn if the person becomes aware of any Inside Information ... (b) suspended upon the start of any Closed Period ... (c) to lapse upon expiration of any time limit for which the approval to trade applies.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A cleared collar trade must be executed within its stated time limit and before any Closed Period or inside information arises, or fresh approval is required.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Canadian SEDI reporting of related financial instruments
bespoke_clauses.clause: a Reporting Insider is required to disclose any change in any interest in, or right or obligation associated with, a related financial instrument. Reporting Insiders must file an insider report electronically through ... 'SEDI', usually within five days after the trade occurs.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As a Canadian-incorporated, dual-listed issuer, a collar entered by a Reporting Insider is likely a 'related financial instrument' requiring its own SEDI filing within about 5 days, additional to and separate from the ASX-side approval and reporting process.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to unvested entitlements, holding locks or equity incentive scheme vesting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no distinct restriction (or exemption) tailored to unvested shares; the collar analysis turns entirely on the general trading-approval and encumbrance-approval provisions regardless of how the shares were acquired.

summary: A funded collar appears achievable under this Policy, which is unusually permissive: there is no hedging-specific prohibition at all, and both encumbering the shares (the loan leg) and entering the derivative legs as ordinary 'trading' are approvable with prior written approval, even inside a Closed Period in exceptional circumstances (hardship, court order or Board discretion) for the encumbrance. Outside Closed Periods, standard prior written approval from the Chair, CEO or Managing Director (or the Audit Committee Chair if the applicant is the Chair) is required, automatically lapses if the person acquires Inside Information or a Closed Period begins, and must be exercised within its stated time limit, so execution should be timed to an open window. A secured lender's enforcement sale on default or margin call is expressly excluded from the Closed Period ban and needs no fresh approval, which reduces the bank's counterparty risk on enforcement. As a Canadian-incorporated dual-listed entity, a Reporting Insider entering the collar will likely also need to file a SEDI report on the resulting 'related financial instrument' within about five days, a disclosure duty separate from the ASX-side clearance process. Directors additionally must report the transaction to the Corporate Secretary within 2 business days for onward 5-business-day ASX disclosure.
